parameters.name: HideSignIns
parameters.description: Leave out the sign-in events (login.success, login.failed, login.locked, login.lockout, logout), which are most of a busy log: "everything except sign-ins". Combines with the other filters.

What to order for one warehouse (AI-02 in its simplest form): the products low there (at or below safety stock, or negative), each topped up to twice its safety level less what is on hand and still on order
(the remaining quantity of the Draft, Submitted and Approved orders of that warehouse, in base units). Rows with nothing to order are not listed. Read-only: to order, create an order with the normal endpoint.
`suggestedValue` (at the warehouse's average cost) is null without `cost.view`. 404 for a warehouse that does not exist or that the caller may not read.

put.summary: Replaces the supplier, the remark and all lines of a Draft. The warehouse cannot change. `If-Match` is required (428 without, 409 when stale).

post.summary: Sends a Draft on. Every line needs a price above 0. When an approval rule fires the order is Submitted and waits for the reviewer of its tier; when none fires it is Approved at once, with no approver. The total at cost is what the rules are tested against.

Approves a Submitted order: the reviewer of its tier (a Supervisor for a standard order, the Owner for a large one, an Administrator either), never the person who submitted it unless self-approval is on.
Returns a Submitted order to Draft with a reason of at least 5 characters, as a review like approving.
Takes the caller's own Submitted order back to Draft (the Edit button): same number, same lines, no reason. Repeating it on an order that is already an ordinary Draft answers 200 and changes nothing.

Cancels a Draft (by its creator), a Submitted order (by its submitter) or an Approved one (by a reviewer it is routed to). The reason is optional, except that cancelling an Approved order needs one of at least 5 characters.

Closes an Approved order short: what is still to come will not come. A reason of at least 5 characters is required, and no receipt of the order may be waiting (Draft, Submitted or Approved): post or
cancel it first. What was received stays. A closed order cannot be received against, and is not reopened by a reversal. An order whose last quantity is received closes itself.

Creates the Draft receipt of an Approved order: the order's warehouse and supplier, one line for every order line that still has something to receive, with the quantity that remains,
the order's unit and the order's price (a caller without `cost.view` gets the receipt without prices, but the stock is valued at them). Each line names its order line in
`purchaseOrderLineNo`. The receipt is then saved, submitted and posted like any other (`/api/documents`); the link never changes. The door is `document.create`; the order must be
readable (`po.read`, checked in the command). 409 when the order is not Approved or has nothing left to receive. The order lists its receipts and what remains.

post.description: Signs in and returns the access token. The refresh token is set as an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to /api/auth. DEPRECATED: only when Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default) is the refresh token also returned in the JSON body; clients must not read it.

Rotates the refresh token and returns a new access token. The refresh token is read from the HttpOnly cookie; the browser must send credentials, the header X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest, and an Origin that is in Cors:Origins (otherwise 403). DEPRECATED: a refreshToken in the request body is still accepted and takes precedence; so is the refresh token in the response body only when Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default).

Revokes the refresh token (from the cookie, or DEPRECATED from the request body) and clears the cookie. Always 204 for an unknown or already revoked token. A cookie-authenticated call needs the same X-Requested-With header and allowed Origin as refresh.

ApprovalMetric.description: What an approval rule measures: the document value or its total quantity.

amountThreshold.description: Money. Null for a caller without `cost.view` (the Warehouse staff), and when the rule has no amount threshold.

roleRequired.description: Deprecated: the system role that holds the tier by default (Supervisor for Standard, Owner for Large), for a client that has not moved to ApproverTier.

oneOf.description: Required (the validator refuses a request without one): the approval a document that fires the rule needs. The deprecated `roleRequired` of earlier releases is no longer read; a client that still sends it is ignored.

ApprovalTriggerDto.description:
One reason a document needs approval: Actual reached Threshold of a rule that asks for ApproverTier.
For an amount rule the two numbers are money, so a caller without `cost.view` (the Warehouse staff) gets them as null: they still see that
the document needs approval and which kind of rule fired (Metric), not the amount. A quantity rule is not hidden.
RoleRequired is deprecated: the system role that holds the tier by default (Supervisor for Standard, Owner for Large).

negativeStockOverrideReason.description: Required when the document `requiresOverride`: why the approver lets stock go below zero. Ignored for any other document.

ApproverTier.description:
Who may satisfy an approval rule: a holder of string Permissions.DocumentApprove (Standard) or of string Permissions.DocumentApproveLarge (Large).
Two levels by design; a third is a new permission and a migration. The values are what the rule stores once it keeps a tier (ADR roles-permissions 4.1).

AssignableRoleDto.description: A role the caller may give to a user: the code the user is saved with and the name people read. No permission list: a user manager need not see what a role holds.

ownerId.description: The public id of the owner: of a document when `OwnerType` is Document, of a product when it is Product.

AttachmentOwnerType.description: What a file is attached to. Adding an owner type means adding one owner policy in the application layer.

AuditFilterOptions.description: What the audit log filters can be offered as dropdowns: the entity names and action names an audit row can carry.

before.description: JSON. A key that names a cost or value is left out for a caller without the permission that unlocks it.

after.description: JSON, with the same rule as Before.

refreshToken.description: DEPRECATED. The refresh token now travels in an HttpOnly cookie; this property is null unless Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default).

AuthResult.description:
The result of a login or refresh. RefreshToken is null when the API is configured to deliver the refresh token
only in its HttpOnly cookie (Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody=false).

reason.description: Why what is still to come will not come: required, at least 5 characters once trimmed.

returnedToMe.description: Drafts I created that a reviewer sent back.

postedToday.description: Documents posted since local midnight (Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, BR-10), whoever posted them, that are still Posted: a document reversed since is not counted, so this equals the Posted list filtered to today.

approvalsWaiting.description: Submitted documents held for approval that I could act on: not mine to approve when self-approval is off, only large ones for the Owner, none large for a Supervisor, zero for roles that cannot approve.

DocumentCounts.description: The numbers behind the Home tiles and menu badges, for the signed-in user, within the warehouses they may see.

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the document was submitted (false for a Draft).

requiresOverride.description: An issue was submitted although stock is short (negative stock is allowed): the approver must give a reason when approving, which forces approval whatever the value thresholds say. A fact about the moment of submission: it stays true after approval and posting; the stored reason is in `NegativeStockOverrideReason`.

isLarge.description: The approval rule that fired needs a role above Supervisor (for example the Owner).

isReturned.description: A Draft that a reviewer sent back (`RejectionReason` holds why, `ReturnedBy*` who).

negativeStockOverrideReason.description: Why the approver let stock go below zero; set when a document that `requiresOverride` is approved, otherwise null.

reversedAt.description: When a Reversed document was reversed, with `ReversedBy` and `ReversedByName` the user who did it ("Reversed by {name} on {date}"); null otherwise. `ReversalReason` holds why.

totalAmount.description: Value of the document: receipts at their entered cost; an issue at its booked cost once posted, and before that at the average cost when it was last saved or submitted (see `AmountIsEstimate`). For a Submitted document this is the value the approval rules were tested against. Null for a caller without `cost.view` (the Warehouse staff).

allowedActions.description: What the caller may do right now (edit, submit, recall, approve, reject, cancel, post, reverse). The UI shows buttons from this list only. It already accounts for ownership (Warehouse staff and Clerk act only on their own documents), the approver the document is routed to (an Owner reviews only `isLarge` documents, a Supervisor the rest) and self-approval, so a listed action is one the API will accept.

approvalTriggers.description: While the document is Submitted or Approved and an approval rule held it back: which thresholds it reaches (value or quantity), for the approver and the "sent for approval" message. Empty otherwise, and when only a negative-stock override (`requiresOverride`) sent it to approval.

oneOf.description: The purchase order this receipt was created from (id and number); null for every other document, and omitted while the Purchasing module is off. Set when the receipt is created and never changed.

amountIsEstimate.description: True for an issue that has not posted yet: its lines carry the average cost seen when it was last saved or submitted, and posting books the real cost. Label the amount "estimated".

concurrencyToken.description: Changes whenever the document (header, status or lines) changes; opaque (a keyed hash bound to this document, not a counter): compare it only for equality. Also sent as the ETag header; send it back as If-Match to refuse a stale save.

unitCost.description: The cost per ENTERED unit (the unit in `UomCode`), in money (2 decimals), that a person TYPED: send it back unchanged to keep the line. For a line whose cost nobody typed (`CostFromAverage`) it is `null`: there is nothing to edit, the line is valued at the average (see `BaseUnitCost` and `Amount`). For a typed cost `qty x unitCost` is the line `amount`. Null for a caller without `cost.view` (the Warehouse staff).

baseUnitCost.description: The cost per BASE unit, for stock valuation, shown as a UNIT PRICE with 4 decimals (not money): a carton price spread over the pieces in it (1 carton of 3 at 10.00 is 3.3333; a carton of 1,000 at 3.00 is 0.0030), or the average for a line at the average. Amounts computed from it are money (2 decimals). Never send it back as `unitCost`. Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

amount.description: The value of the line, in money, stored when the line was saved: `round(qty x unitCost, 2)` for a typed cost, `round(baseQty x average, 2)` for a line at the average. It is the only figure to add up: a document total is the sum of the line `amount`s (never `qty x unitCost` of the lines: that is wrong for a line at the average). Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

costFromAverage.description: Nobody typed this line's cost: it is valued at the average cost of the product (every issue line; a receipt line saved by someone who may not enter cost, such as the Warehouse staff). It has no editable cost (`unitCost` is null), and saving the draft without a cost for it keeps it at the average; typing a cost makes it a typed cost. Show its `amount` and `baseUnitCost` read-only. On a draft its amount is re-valued at the current average on every save and at post, so a draft read earlier can be stale.

available.description: On hand in the document's warehouse right now, in base units (compare with `BaseQty`; lines of one product add up). Null once the document is Posted, Reversed or Cancelled, when the figure no longer says anything about this document.

purchaseOrderLineNo.description: On a receipt created from a purchase order: the order line this line receives (its `lineNo`); null otherwise, and omitted while the Purchasing module is off. Send it back unchanged when saving the draft.

Only on a receipt created from a purchase order (`POST /api/purchase-orders/{id}/receipt`): the `lineNo` of the purchase order line this line receives. Every line of such a receipt must name one (a save without it is a 400 and the link is kept), the line's product and unit must be the order line's, and the quantities named for one order line must not exceed what remains of it. On any other document it must be left out (a 400 otherwise), and it is a 400 "not available" while the Purchasing module is off. The link itself is never sent and never changes: it is set when the receipt is created.

totalAmount.description: Same meaning as on the full document: an unposted issue is valued at the average cost seen when it was last saved or submitted (`AmountIsEstimate`). Null for a caller without `cost.view` (the Warehouse staff).

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the document was submitted. With `status=Submitted` this is the approvals inbox.

isReturned.description: A Draft that a reviewer sent back.

concurrencyToken.description: Same value as `concurrencyToken` on the full document: compare it to know whether an open document has gone stale.

amountIsEstimate.description: True for an issue that has not posted yet: `totalAmount` is an estimate at the average cost seen when it was last saved or submitted.

canAct.description:
The caller may approve or reject this document right now: it is Submitted and held for approval, routed to the caller's role
(an Owner reviews only `isLarge` documents, a Supervisor the rest, an Admin all) and, unless self-approval is on, not submitted by the caller.
This is exactly the rule behind the "waiting for approval" count. A single document's `allowedActions` additionally tests the live approval rules.

DocumentStatus.description: Figure 5 state machine. Rejection returns to Draft (reason kept on the document).

DocumentType.description:
The kind of a document, and the subject an ApprovalRule is written for. DocumentType.PurchaseOrder and DocumentType.SalesOrder are not stock documents (an order is its own aggregate and
moves no stock, plans PL2 D2 and PL3 D1): it is here only so that the approval rules and their two tiers are reused for it. StockDocument StockDocument.Create(DocumentType type, Warehouse warehouse, Partner? partner, IssuePurpose? purpose, string? remark, int createdBy, DateTime now) refuses it and StockDirection
has no direction for it.

created.description: Rows that create (a preview reports what a commit would create).

updated.description: Rows that update an existing record (a preview reports what a commit would update).

documentId.description: The public id of the first draft receipt a committed opening-stock import created; null for a preview and for other imports.

ok.description: False when the row has errors and blocks the import.

status.description: New or Update for a valid row (what a commit would do with it; the same in a preview and after a commit), Error otherwise. A valid row can still carry a note in `Errors` (for example "unit not changed").

ImportRowStatus.description: What an import row does (or would do on commit): create something new, update something that exists, or nothing because it has errors.

unitCost.description: Cost per base unit of the movement. Null for a caller without `valuation.view`.

balanceAfter.description: What this product held in this warehouse right after the movement (the sum of its ledger up to and including this row, in base units). Only given when the ledger is read for one product (`productId`); null otherwise (a list of several products has no single running balance). Stored with the row when it is written (under the same lock that serialises the postings of the product in the warehouse), so reading any page, however deep, costs the same and the answer cannot be overtaken by a posting.

LinkedPurchaseOrder.description: The purchase order a receipt was created from: its id and number. Omitted while the Purchasing module is off.

warehouseId.description: Null (with the code and the name) only for a product stocked in no warehouse the caller can see. It appears ONCE, not once per warehouse.

qtyOnHand.description: Zero for a product that is stocked in no warehouse the caller can see (it has no balance row there: it is listed once, with no warehouse). Negative when stock went below zero.

shortfall.description: Safety stock minus on hand: how many units are missing (more than the safety level when the balance is negative).

isNegative.description: On hand is below zero: show it as a warning, not just as "low".

ModuleDto.description: A module and whether this installation has it on. `Requires` lists the codes of modules that must be on first (none yet).

ModuleSwitchRequest.description: Turn a module on or off. `Enabled` has no default on purpose: a body that leaves it out is a 400, never a quiet switch off. The reason is kept in the audit log.

rolesRegainingGrants.description: Live roles that hold at least one permission of the module and so have it in force again.

ModuleSwitchResult.description:
What a module switch answers: the module as `GET /api/modules` lists it, plus how many roles got permissions back. A module's permissions are kept, hidden, on the roles that
hold them while it is off; turning it on gives them back at once, so this count is the warning. It is 0 when the module was turned off, was already in the state asked for, or
has no permissions.

postedAt.description: When the movement happened: the posting time, or for a reversal row the time of the reversal.

qty.description: As entered, unsigned, in the line's own unit. Unchanged by decimal MovementRow.StockEffect.

baseQty.description: Unsigned, in the product's base unit.

stockEffect.description: Signed, in base units: positive when the movement adds stock, negative when it removes stock. A receipt adds, an issue removes, and the reversal row of a document does the opposite of its posting. Summed over a product and a period (a date range on `PostedAt`) it equals the change in the product's stock balance.

unitCost.description: Per base unit. Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

amount.description: Base quantity times unit cost. Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

isReversal.description: The row is the reversal of the posting shown in the row for the same document and line.

MovementRow.description: One line of the receipt/issue detail. A document reversed since posting has two rows per line: the posting and the reversal.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `cursor` for the next page of a seek-paged list; null when there is no further page or the list is not seek-paged. Clients never parse it.

adminCore.description: The Administrator role always holds it.

requires.description: Codes that must be granted together with this one (a role that has this code without them is refused).

module.description: The module the permission belongs to, or null for a core permission. The list only holds permissions of modules that are on, so a client needs it only to label the entry.

PermissionDto.description: One permission of the catalog, as the role editor lists it.

PermissionGroup.description: The sections of the permission catalog, in the order the role editor lists them.

ProductLookupResult.description:
Answer to a barcode or SKU lookup. A code nobody owns is a normal outcome of scanning, not an error:
`Found` is false and `Product` is null (HTTP 200), so a scan miss does not look like a failed request.

ProductSort.description: Sort keys the products list accepts. Only these are allowed, so a client cannot sort on an unindexed column.

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the order was submitted (false for a Draft, and for an order released at once because no rule fired).

isLarge.description: The rule that fired needs the large tier (the Owner), not a Supervisor.

isReturned.description: A Draft that a reviewer sent back (`RejectionReason` holds why, `ReturnedBy*` who).

closedAt.description: When a Closed order was closed; null otherwise.

oneOf.description: How it was closed: `Received` (the last quantity was received, by posting) or `Short` (a person closed it with `closeReason`). Null while not Closed.

closeReason.description: Why a person closed the order short (5 or more characters); null for any other order.

totalQty.description: The total base quantity: what a quantity rule of the approval rules is tested against.

totalAmount.description: The sum of the line amounts, in money. Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

concurrencyToken.description: Changes whenever the order (header, status or lines) changes; opaque: compare it only for equality. Also sent as the ETag header; send it back as If-Match to refuse a stale save.

receipts.description: The receipts created from this order, oldest first (number, state), whatever their state. Empty until the order is Approved. The quantities per line (`receivedQty`, `remainingQty`) count the Posted ones only.

unitPrice.description: The price per ENTERED unit (the unit in `UomCode`), in money. Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

amount.description: The value of the line, in money: `round(qty x unitPrice, 2)`. The order total is the sum of these. Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

receivedQty.description: What Posted receipts linked to the order have received of this line, in `uomCode`. Computed on every read, never stored: a Draft, Submitted, Approved or Cancelled receipt counts as nothing, and so does a Reversed one. Zero until a receipt is posted.

remainingQty.description: What is still to receive of this line, in `uomCode`: `qty` minus `receivedQty`, never below zero. A receipt may not ask for more than this.

receivedBaseQty.description: `receivedQty` in base units: the unit the ledger and the over-receipt check use.

qty.description: In the unit named by `uomId`; at most 4 decimal places.

uomId.description: Any unit the product converts to its base unit; null means the base unit.

unitPrice.description: The price per ENTERED unit, in money (at most 2 decimal places, never negative). 0.00 is accepted on a draft; the workflow slice refuses to submit it.

totalAmount.description: The sum of the line amounts, in money. Null for a caller without `cost.view`.

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the order was submitted. With `status=Submitted` these are the orders waiting for a reviewer.

isLarge.description: The rule that fired needs the large tier (the Owner).

concurrencyToken.description: Same value as `concurrencyToken` on the full order: compare it to know whether an open order has gone stale.

canAct.description:
The caller may approve or reject this order right now: it is Submitted and held for approval, routed to the caller's tier (the Owner reviews only `isLarge` orders, a
Supervisor the rest, an Administrator all) and, unless self-approval is on, not submitted by the caller. A single order's `allowedActions` additionally tests the live rules.

PurchaseOrderReceiptDto.description: A receipt created from a purchase order, as the order lists it: its id (for the receipt screen), number and state. No money.

warehouseId.description: The ship-to warehouse. It cannot change after the order is created: it carries the number.

supplierId.description: An active partner of type Supplier.

PurchaseOrderSaveRequest.description: A whole purchase-order draft: every field is sent on every save (there is no "absent = unchanged"), and the lines replace the old ones. The same product may appear on several lines (different units, prices or remarks): anything that refers to a line, such as receiving against the order (PL2.4, PL2.5), must use its line number, never the product.

PurchaseOrderStatus.description:
The stored state of a purchase order. Draft is the only state a caller can reach before the approval workflow exists (pilot slice PL2.3); "partly received" and "fully received" are
derived labels, never stored. An order is open (it blocks switching the purchasing module off) while it is Draft, Submitted or Approved.

refreshToken.description: DEPRECATED. The refresh token now travels in an HttpOnly cookie; this property is null unless Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default).

RefreshRequest.description: The refresh token to redeem or revoke. Optional on the wire: when absent, the API reads it from the HttpOnly cookie.

qtyOnHand.description: Zero for a product that is stocked in no warehouse the caller can see; negative when stock went below zero.

onOrderQty.description: Still to come on the open orders (Draft, Submitted, Approved) of this warehouse: ordered less posted receipts, line by line.

suggestedQty.description: Twice the safety level less on hand less on order; always above zero (a row with nothing to order is not listed).

suggestedValue.description: The suggested quantity at the warehouse's average cost, in money. Null for a caller without `cost.view`, and for a product with no average cost yet (never stocked).

ReorderSuggestion.description: One product to order for one warehouse (see ReorderRule). Quantities are in the product's base unit. The product has no preferred supplier in the data model, so the buyer chooses one.

copyFromRoleId.description: Takes the permissions the other role holds now (no link is kept).

RoleCreateRequest.description: A new custom role. The code is made by the server from the name. Give CopyFromRoleId or Permissions, not both; neither makes a blank role.

id.description: The public id; the only id a client ever sees.

code.description: Stable, never changes; the text a user is saved with.

permissions.description: The permission codes the role holds, in catalog order.

userCount.description: Live users who hold the role, active or not: what blocks a deletion or a deactivation.

concurrencyToken.description: Changes whenever the role or its permissions change; opaque. Also sent as the ETag header; send it back as If-Match.

RolePermissionsRequest.description: The whole set of permissions the role is to hold (a replace, not a patch).

RolePermissionsResult.description: The role after a replace, and what the replace changed (both empty when the set was the same).

RoleUpdateRequest.description: The text and the state of a role. Its code, its kind and its permissions are not here. A description or state that is left out stays as it is.

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the order was submitted (false for a Draft, and for an order released at once because no rule fired).

isLarge.description: The rule that fired needs the large tier (the Owner), not a Supervisor.

isReturned.description: A Draft that a reviewer sent back (`RejectionReason` holds why, `ReturnedBy*` who).

totalQty.description: The total base quantity: what a quantity rule of the approval rules is tested against.

totalAmount.description: The sum of the line amounts, in money. Absent for a caller without `so.manage`: a selling price is not cost, so `cost.view` is not what decides it.

concurrencyToken.description: Changes whenever the order (header, status or lines) changes; opaque: compare it only for equality. Also sent as the ETag header; send it back as If-Match to refuse a stale save.

amount.description: The value of the line, in money: `round(qty x unitPrice, 2)`. The order total is the sum of these. Absent for a caller without `so.manage`.

qty.description: In the unit named by `uomId`; at most 4 decimal places.

uomId.description: Any unit the product converts to its base unit; null means the base unit.

unitPrice.description: The price per ENTERED unit, in money (at most 2 decimal places, never negative). 0.00 is accepted on a draft; submitting it is refused (PL3.3).

totalAmount.description: The sum of the line amounts, in money. Absent for a caller without `so.manage`.

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the order was submitted. With `status=Submitted` these are the orders waiting for a reviewer.

isLarge.description: The rule that fired needs the large tier (the Owner).

concurrencyToken.description: Same value as `concurrencyToken` on the full order: compare it to know whether an open order has gone stale.

canAct.description:
The caller may approve or reject this order right now: it is Submitted and held for approval, routed to the caller's tier (the Owner reviews only `isLarge` orders, a
Supervisor the rest, an Administrator all) and, unless self-approval is on, not submitted by the caller. A single order's `allowedActions` additionally tests the live rules.

warehouseId.description: The ship-from warehouse. It cannot change after the order is created: it carries the number.

customerId.description: An active partner of type Customer.

SalesOrderSaveRequest.description: A whole sales-order draft: every field is sent on every save (there is no "absent = unchanged"), and the lines replace the old ones. The same product may appear on several lines (different units, prices or remarks): anything that refers to a line, such as delivering against the order (PL3.5), must use its line number, never the product.

SalesOrderStatus.description:
The stored state of a sales order. "Partly delivered" is a derived label, never stored. An order is open (it blocks switching the sales module off) while it is Draft, Submitted or Approved.
Only Draft is reachable until the workflow slice (PL3.3); the other values are in place so that slice needs no migration.

warehouseId.description: Null (with the code and the name) only on the low-only row of a product that has no stock in any warehouse the caller can see: it is listed once, belongs to no warehouse and has quantity 0.

avgCost.description: Average cost per base unit. Null for a caller without `valuation.view`, and for a product stocked in no warehouse the caller can see (a low-stock row with nothing on hand: there is no average, which is not an average of zero).

value.description: Quantity on hand times average cost. Null for a caller without `valuation.view`, and for a product stocked in no warehouse the caller can see.

isLow.description: Low by the one definition (LowStockRule): the product is active and its quantity is below zero, or at or below its safety stock (when it has one; design 3.8, "on-hand <= safety stock"). The low-stock list, its count, the Home tile and the badge use the same rule.

isNegative.description: On hand is below zero: show a warning, not just a "Low" chip (also true when the product has no safety stock).

StockSort.description: `Value` orders by quantity times average cost, which would reveal the value to a caller who may not see it: it needs `valuation.view` (otherwise 400).

totalValue.description: Net value of the stock in the caller's warehouses (quantity x average cost). A negative balance lowers it, so it can be less than the sum of the positive lines. Null for a caller without `valuation.view`.

skuCount.description: Products with stock: distinct products that have a positive quantity in at least one of the caller's warehouses (zero and negative balances are not counted).

lowCount.description: Product x warehouse pairs on the low-stock list (see `GET /api/stock/low-stock`): at or below safety stock, stocked in no visible warehouse (counted once) with a safety level, or negative. Equals that list's total.

UserInfo.description:
The signed-in user. `Permissions` lists the codes of the access token (the role's grants when it was issued) in catalog order; the web reads it for menus and
buttons, the API decides by the token itself. `Modules` lists the codes of the modules this installation has on (read when the answer is built, not carried by the token), in catalog order.

role.description: The code of a role in the Role table (a system role or a custom one).

allWarehouses.description: Sees every warehouse whatever WarehouseIds says. Left out: unchanged on an update, false for a new user.

Bearer.description: Paste the access token from POST /api/auth/login (without the word Bearer).
